For that patient, the bath [is prescribed] during the *cara* (movable) *bhāgas*, during the *cara* *nakṣatras* beginning with Svāti, in the three *harit* (green/young) *nakṣatras*, in the *cara* *lagnas* of Aries, Cancer, Libra, and Capricorn, on Sundays and Tuesdays (*sūryabhauma-vāra*), on the *rikta* lunar days, in the dark fortnight (*kṛṣṇapakṣa*), and here too when the Moon is auspicious. As stated in the *Ratnamālā*: "On a *rikta* lunar day, when the strength of the Moon is lacking"—here, "strength of the Moon" refers to its inherent (*naisargika*) strength; thus, the meaning is "when the Moon is waning."

In that regard, one should avoid Friday and Monday; the fixed asterisms (Dhruva-māni); Āśleṣā (Sarpa), Revatī (Pauṣṇa), Maghā (Pitṛ-maṇḍala), Punarvasu (Āditya), and Svātī (Anila-kṣa). [41] The *saṃkrānti* (transits): *Ghorā* occurs when the Sun is in a cruel sign and the Moon is in a cruel sign; *Dhyāṅkṣī* occurs when the Sun is in an even sign and the Moon is in an odd sign; likewise, *Mahodarī* occurs when the Sun is in an odd sign and the Moon is in an even sign. On the days of Mars and Mercury, it is *Mandākinī*; on the days of Jupiter and the fixed asterisms (*dhruva*), it is *Mandā*. Because of the mention of "mixed" (*miśra*) with Venus, it is *Miśrā*; and on the day of Saturn, it is *Tīkṣṇā*. *Rākṣasī* is excellent for Śūdras, Kavis (poets), Vaiśyas, thieves, kings, Brahmins, and those of low birth, respectively. [42] Regarding the verse beginning with *ghorā*: "Ghorā" occurs when the Sun is in a cruel sign and the Moon is in a cruel sign; "Dhyāṅkṣī" occurs when the Sun is in an even sign and the Moon is in an odd sign; likewise, "Mahodarī" occurs when the Sun is in an odd sign and the Moon is in an even sign. On the days of Mars and Mercury, it is "Mandākinī"; on the days of Jupiter and the fixed asterisms (*dhruva*), it is "Mandā. Because of the mention of "mixed" (*miśra*) with Venus, it is "Miśrā"; and on the day of Saturn, it is "Tīkṣṇā. "Rākṣasī" is excellent for Śūdras, Kavis (poets), Vaiśyas, thieves, kings, Brahmins, and those of low birth, respectively. [42] *Saṭīkā* (with commentary). "Mandā" [is auspicious] for mixed [castes], and because of the mention of "mixed," [it applies to others]; "Tīkṣṇā" [is for] the son of Saturn (Saturn); "Rākṣasī" is excellent for Śūdras, Kavis, Vaiśyas, thieves, kings, Brahmins, and those of low birth, respectively. [42] *Ghorā* etc. [End of commentary].

A transit occurring on a Sunday in the *krūra* (cruel) signs is called *ghorā*; in the *laghu* (light) signs on a Monday, it is *dhvāṅkṣī*; a transit occurring on a Tuesday (*kṣoṇīja*) in the *cara* (movable) signs is *mahodarī*; in the *mṛdu* (soft) signs on a Wednesday, it is *mandākinī*; in the *dhruva* (fixed) signs on a Thursday (*ijya*), it is *mandā*; and a transit in the *miśra* (mixed) signs on a Friday (*sita*)— [is called *mandā*].

That [transit] becomes mixed; the transit that occurs on a Saturday during the sharp (tīkṣṇa) periods is named Rākṣasī. Thus, when two names are complete due to the simultaneous conjunction of day and weekday, it is so; otherwise, if the name differs due to the influence of a single factor, then there are two names. In sequence, all seven transits are auspicious for Śūdras, Vaiśyas, thieves, Kṣatriyas, twice-born (Dvijas), cattle, and Mlecchas respectively.

Ghorā brings happiness to Śūdras; Dhvāṅkṣī brings happiness to Vaiśyas; Mahodarī brings happiness to thieves; Mandākinī brings happiness to kings; Mandā brings happiness to the twice-born (Brāhmaṇas); Mitrā brings happiness to animals; and Rākṣasī brings happiness to outcasts. The auspicious times for the Saṃkrāntis (the Sun’s passage into a new zodiac sign) are as follows: two *nāḍīs* (forty-eight minutes) are auspicious during the Ṣaḍaśīti, the retrograde motion (*vakrama*), and the northern course (*uttarāyaṇa*). In Capricorn (*mṛga*) and the subsequent signs, sixteen *nāḍīs* are auspicious. Likewise, sixteen *nāḍīs* are auspicious at the equinoxes (*viṣuva*) in Aries (*meṣa*) and Libra (*taulina*).

The midday [transits] in a fixed sign are most meritorious; the southern transit in Cancer is auspicious, and the forenoon transits therein are also most meritorious. One should offer sesame, milk, grain, and ghee. (43) [From the *Muhūrtadīpaka*]: "Śaṅgaḥ" means this: the transit that occurs in a dual-natured (*dvisvabhāva*) sign is called a "Ṣaḍaśītimukha. The dual-natured signs are Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, and Pisces; these are designated as the "mouths of the Ṣaḍaśītis. The transit that occurs in Capricorn (*mṛga*) is the northern transit (*saumyāyana*).

In this context, regarding the five transits (*saṃkrānti*), the sixteen *nāḍīs* (or *ghaṭikās*) following the time of the northern transit (*uttarā saṃkrāntiḥ*) are merit-bestowing. This has been stated generally: "Sixteen *ghaṭikās* are meritorious times, both before and after the transit," according to such scriptural authority. Otherwise, a specific distinction for these two has been stated in the *Brahmavaivarta Purāṇa* and other texts: "The past and future [periods] are meritorious during both the northern and southern solstices (*ayana*)."

"Thirty *nāḍīs* in Cancer, but in Capricorn they are ten more. Thus, forty *ghaṭikās* are stated for Capricorn. Likewise, in Aries and Libra—that is, during the transits (*saṃkrānti*) of Aries and Libra—at the equinoxes (*viṣuvatyām*), the middle [periods] are most meritorious; yet, due to a specific statement, ten [periods] are declared [to be meritorious] on both sides. This is because of the statement: "In the current [transits] of Libra and Aries, there are ten *nāḍīs* on both sides. In the fixed signs (*sthira-rāśi*)—the transits of Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, and Aquarius—the term "Hari's step" (*haripada*) occurs.

In Cancer, the southern solstice occurs. Therein, the thirty *nāḍīs* prior to the transit (*saṃkrānti*) are merit-bestowing. At that time of the transit, one should offer sesame seeds, grain, and ghee. Thus it has been said by Vyāsa: "O Bhārata, whatever gifts, offerings to the gods (*havya*), or offerings to the ancestors (*kavya*) are given during a transit, each of those accrues to the ancestors and becomes inexhaustible. (43) [The signs] Capricorn, Leo, Taurus, and Libra [are the fixed signs]. The acts concerning elephants, horses, and cows [should be performed in these].

The work for elephants is [prescribed] during the two Āditya [nakṣatras], and for horses during the two Pauṣṇa [nakṣatras]. Likewise, for deer it is during the pair Svāti and Jyeṣṭhā; for cattle, during the pair Mṛgaśiras and Ardrā; and for goats, during the pair Śakra (Jyeṣṭhā) and Ārdrā, as well as the two Vasu [nakṣatras] and the pair of Āditi (Punarvasu). For cows, it is during the pair Dhaniṣṭhā and Aśvinī, and during Revatī and Puṣya. And for donkeys, it is during the pair of Kṛttikā and Rohiṇī, and during the eighth lunar day (Riktā) and the Sun (Sunday). [Commentary: Regarding the verse beginning with "dvayāditya": The work for elephants is performed under the two Āditya nakṣatras (Pūrvaphalgunī and Uttaraphalgunī). For horses, it is under the two Pauṣṇa nakṣatras (Revatī and Aśvinī). Similarly, for deer, it is under the pair Svāti and Jyeṣṭhā; for cattle, under the pair Mṛgaśiras and Ardrā; and for goats, under the pair Śakra (Jyeṣṭhā) and Ārdrā, as well as the two Vasu nakṣatras (Dhruva = Rohiṇī and Śravaṇa) and the pair of Āditi (Punarvasu). For cows, it is under the pair Dhaniṣṭhā and Aśvinī, and under Revatī and Puṣya. And for donkeys, it is under the pair of Kṛttikā and Rohiṇī, and on the eighth lunar day (Riktā) and when the Sun is present (on Sunday). [Note: The term *kariṇām* refers to elephants; *mṛgavamu* refers to deer; *gāḥ* refers to cows; *karṇa* refers to donkeys.]

In these yogas, the work of elephants—such as mounting, leading, and training—should be performed. In which [asterisms]? In Āditya (Pūrvaphalgunī), Āviḥ (Uttaraphalgunī), Vyāditya (Punarvasu), and Puṣya; there, in Aśvin (Aśvinī), Karatraya (Hasta, Citrā, Svāti)—one should perform the work of elephants. Furthermore, in Pauṣṇadvaya (Revatī and Aśvinī), Svāti, Īdhye (Jyeṣṭhā), Puṣya, Aditibha (Pūrvaphalgunī), Punarvasu, Kara (Hasta), Mṛga (Mṛgaśīrṣa), and Vasudvanda (Dhaniṣṭhā and Śatabhiṣaj), one should perform the work of horses—namely, leading, mounting, and other training exercises.

In the Śaka year, under the asterisms of Jyeṣṭhā when the Sun is in Hasta, under the two Aṣṭakas (the eighth lunar days) of the Vasus (the eighth house), under Dhaniṣṭhā and Śatabhiṣaj, under Aditi’s pair (Punarvasu and Puṣya), under Dvīśa (Viśākhā), Viśākhā, Aśvinī, and Pauṣṇa (Revatī), one should perform such acts as bringing in cattle and bulls, as well as their purchase, sale, taming, and other related rites.

On the asterisms of Karṇa (Śravaṇa), Dhruva (Uttarā-phalgunī), Rohiṇī, and the Uttarās; on the two junctions of the lunar fortnights—the new moon (darśa) and the full moon (paurṇamāsī); on the eighth day of the fortnight; on the asterism of Tvāṣṭra (Citrā); on the "empty" lunar days (riktātithi); and on Sunday—no work whatsoever should be performed regarding animals, such as horses and cattle, according to the previously mentioned method. As it has been said: "A wise man should never perform the entering of a stable or the departure [of animals] under Citrā, the Uttarās, Śraviṣṭhā, or Rohiṇī, nor on the fourteenth day, the new moon day, or the eighth day. (44)

Three [marks] on the wheel and the head bring happiness; three on the face bestow honor; five on the chest lead to prosperity; eight on the feet cause misfortune; four on the tail bring about one's own ruin; and four on the back [result in death]. Some say this is the result of the Sun and other planets according to their positions in the zodiacal signs. (45) [Regarding the verse beginning with] "On the wheel": "Cakra" refers to the wheel-mark. "Aśve" means on the horse. "Śirasi" means on the head. "Trayam" means three marks. "Sukhakara" means producing happiness. "Vakre" means on the face. "Mānadam" means bestowing honor. "Vṛddhaye" means for the sake of increase or prosperity. "Pañca" means five. "Hṛdistham" means situated on the chest. "Āni" refers to the joints or specific spots. "Caraṇeṣu" means on the feet. "Aṣṭau" means eight. "Tu" is a particle used for emphasis. "Duṣṭāni" means harmful or evil results. "Pucche" means on the tail. "Svakṣayakṛt" means causing one's own destruction. "Catuṣṭayam" means a group of four. "Atho" means then or furthermore. "Pṛṣṭhe" means on the back. "Catuṣkam" means a group of four. "Mṛtau" means at the time of death. "Sūryādinabhāvadheḥ" means from the Sun and other planets according to their respective signs (rāśis). "Phalamidam" means this result. "Vāhakṣataḥ" means arising from the horse. "Kecana" means some [authorities]. ||45|| "Cakre" etc. [End of commentary].

In the "Horse" (Aśva) yoga, three asterisms should be assigned to the head on the horse-shaped wheel; in this moment, they bring happiness. Then three in the face grant honor. Then five asterisms in the heart lead to prosperity for the increase of the vehicle. Then eight asterisms in the four legs are considered unfavorable—thus says the *Muhūrtadīpaka*.

If there are four [asterisms] in the tail (puccha), they cause one's own destruction; if there are four in the back (pṛṣṭha), it is a sign of death—thus some say these are the results based on the asterism occupied by the Sun and other planets. Others, however, state that the result is based on the asterism occupied by the horse's rider (bāhaka). But that is not so; for in the *Jayacaryā*, at the time of battle, one marks the position of the horse for the purpose of observing the placement of Saturn. Here, however, the calculation must be made from the asterism occupied by the Sun itself. || 45 ||

The water-offering [to the deity] is performed under the asterisms of Mṛgaśīrṣa, Revatī, Hasta, Punarvasu, Viśākhā, the two Dhaniṣṭhās, the three Pūrvas, and Śatabhiṣaj. Furthermore, the work of camels and buffaloes, as well as the churning [of curds], is auspicious in Mūla, Revatī, the three Hastas, the fixed asterisms (Dhruva), Mṛgaśīrṣa, Anurādhā, Śravaṇa, and Dhaniṣṭhā. The water-offering is performed on the days of Mercury, Jupiter, and Venus, as well as in Mūla, Hasta, and Śravaṇa. Regarding the word "Saumya" [in verse 46]: in these aforementioned yogas, the work of camels is auspicious.

Among these, in which [constellations] should the work of tethering, buying, and selling camels, as well as the bringing and milking of buffaloes, be performed? In the gentle [asterisms]: Mṛgaśīrṣa, the pair of Pauṣṇa (Revatī and Aśvinī), Revatī and Aśvinī, Hasta, the pair of Aditi (Punarvasu), the two Viśākhās, Viśākhā, the pair of Dhaniṣṭhā (Dhaniṣṭhā and Śatabhiṣaj), the three Pūrvās, the pair of Indra (Jyeṣṭhā and Mūla), and Jyeṣṭhā and Mūla. In these, the work of tethering, buying, and selling camels, as well as the bringing and milking of buffaloes, should be undertaken.

Now, regarding the auspicious moment for churning curd (*dadhimanthana-muhūrta*): one should undertake the new beginning of churning curd under the asterisms of Mūla, Pūṣan (Revatī), the three Kṛttikās, Hasta, Citrā, Svātī, the fixed stars (the three Uttaras), Rohiṇī, Mṛgaśiras, Maitra (Anurādhā), Aśvinī, Vāsava (Dhaniṣṭhā), and Dhaniṣṭhā itself.

Then, the worship of the Water-Mothers (Jalamātṛs) should be performed by women who have given birth with water-offerings; that water-worship is [recommended] on the days of the Moon, Jupiter, and Venus, under the asterisms Mūla, Hasta, Śravaṇa, and Vaiṣṇava (Śatabhiṣaj), or otherwise according to family custom. [The Muhūrta for digging a well, with commentary: In the months of Phālguna, Pauṣa, Māgha, Nabhas (Śrāvaṇa), and Mārgaśīrṣa, avoiding the eighth, twelfth, and "empty" (Riktā) lunar days, and on the days of Mercury, Jupiter, and Venus, under the asterisms Hasta, Anurādhā (Maitra), and the Dhruva group (Uttarā-phalgunī, Uttarā-āṣāḍhā, and Uttarā-bhādrapadā).

In the months of Phālguna, Pauṣa, Vaiśākha, Śrāvaṇa, and Mārgaśīrṣa, the construction of a well is most excellent when Saturn, Mercury, and Jupiter are in the ascendant or the Karkini [Navāṃśa], provided that the benefic planets are situated in the quadrants (kendras) or the trines (trikoṇas). (47) Regarding the "months": among these conjunctions, the procedure for constructing a well is best. In which ones? In the months of Phālguna, Pauṣa, Vaiśākha, Śrāvaṇa, and Mārgaśīrṣa. Therein, one should exclude and abandon the eighth, twelfth, and the Riktā tithis.

On the day of the Moon (Śaśin), Mercury (Jña), or Jupiter (Jīva); under the asterism Hasta, Svātī, Mṛgaśīrṣa, Rohiṇī, the three Uttaras, Puṣya, Anurādhā, Dhaniṣṭhā, or Śatabhiṣaj; during the planetary periods of Saturn, Mercury, or Jupiter; when the Ascendant (Lagna) is occupied by Saturn, Mercury, or Jupiter; and when benefic planets are situated in the quadrants (1st, 4th, 7th, 10th) or the trines (5th and 9th)—at such times, the commencement of digging a well should be performed. (47)

The auspicious time for digging a well and planting trees: One should dig a water-well having avoided the directions of Wind (Vāyu), Fire (Hutāśa), and Rākṣasa (Nairṛti) from the village. One should draw a diagram starting from the center toward the direction of Indra (East), marking the positions of the Sun and others in their successive order. For the planting of trees, the directions from the center toward the North (Saumya), West (Varuṇa), and Southeast (Āgneya) are auspicious. The asterisms Puṣya, the Mṛdu group, Citrā, Aśvinī, Śatabhiṣaj, Viśākhā, and Mūla, along with Hasta, are suitable. [From the verse]: "From the village... etc.

Leaving aside the northwest, southeast, and southwest corners from the village, one should dig a water-well in the southwest (rākṣasa) corner for the purpose of filling it with water. Regarding that wheel of the well (*kūpacakra*), the *Muhūrtadīpaka* states: One should write down the asterisms starting from the Sun's asterism (*arkabha*) in groups of three, proceeding in order from the center toward the directions of Indra (east), and so on. Therein, the calculation should be made up to the asterism of the auspicious moment (*muhūrta*). Those situated in the center, the north, the west, and the southeast are auspicious.

If the auspicious *muhūrta* and *nakṣatra* fall at midday, it is favorable; it is excellent in the northern direction (the quarter of Soma), excellent in the western direction (the quarter of Varuṇa), and also excellent in the north-eastern corner (*āmayakoṇa*).

Now, regarding the planting of trees: Puṣya is excellent for the planting of trees. The *mṛdu* [nakṣatras]—Citrā, Revatī, Anurādhā, and Mṛgaśiras—are excellent, as are the fixed (*dhruva*) nakṣatras—Rohiṇī, the three Uttarās, Aśvinī, Śatabhiṣaj (Śatam), Viśākhā, and Mūla along with Kṛttikā (Kara). Trees should be planted under these; the sowing of seeds for the tree should be performed [under these same asterisms]. 48. The *muhūrta* for the consecration of deities.

In the Anurādhā, Revatī, Aśvinī, Abhijit, Mṛgaśīrṣa, the two Śravaṇas, Rohiṇī, Puṣya, and the two Āśleṣās; avoiding the Riktā tithis, the Viṣṭi karaṇa, and Tuesday; with benefic planets situated in the ninth, third, tenth, and eleventh houses, and malefic planets situated in the fifth and eighth houses; and when Jupiter is fixed (not retrograde)—in these yogas, the installation of Hari should take place. Regarding the verse beginning with "maitra": in these aforementioned configurations, the installation of Hari shall be performed.

The installation of Hari should be performed under these asterisms: Anurādhā, Revatī (Pauṣṇa), the light signs (laghubha)—Hasta, Puṣya, Aśvinī, and Abhijit; the fixed signs (dhruva)—Rohiṇī, the three Uttarās, and Punarvasu (Aditi-bha); and Mṛgaśīrṣa (Mṛga), the two Karṇas (Śravaṇa and Dhaniṣṭhā). In these, the consecration of Hari takes place.

The installation of the images and other representations of Vāgdevī Sarasvatī, Gaṇanāyaka Gaṇeśa, the serpents (Nāgas), the Kṣetrapālas and others should take place under the asterisms of Śravaṇa, Dhaniṣṭhā, Pūṣa (Revatī), and Revatī. Under the worshipful Puṣya, the fixed (dhruva) asterisms—Rohiṇī and the three Uttaras (Uttarāphalgunī, Uttarāṣāḍhā, and Uttarābhādrapadā)—that is, in these four fixed asterisms. Regarding the installation therein, he states the planetary conjunctions: nine (9), five (5), and the angles (1, 4, 7).

With auspicious planets in the tenth, eleventh, and first houses, and malefic planets situated in the sixth, third, and eleventh houses, one should perform the installation (*pratiṣṭhāpana*). Having avoided the *riktā* tithis (the 4th, 9th, and 14th), the *viṣṭi* karana, and Tuesday (*kuja*), the installation of images should be carried out. (49) Dancing, royal inspection, service, and the commencement of liquor should be undertaken during the auspicious moments of the asterisms of Revatī (*pauṣṇa*), Puṣya, the two Vasus (Pūrvā-phalgunī and Uttara-phalgunī), the Sun’s sign (Āśleṣā), Anurādhā (*maitra*), and the three Uttarās (Uttarā-phalgunī, Uttarā-āṣāḍhā, and Uttarā-bhādrapadā). Dancing and royal inspection should be performed under these.

In the two asterisms of Śravaṇā and Śatabhiṣaj, which are light, soft, auspicious, and stable, the protection of servants is recommended for one of firm body. On the day of Saturn (Śanivāra), in the fixed asterisms of Pūrvaphalgunī, Ārdrā, Puṣya, Mūla, and Śatabhiṣaj, and in the southern asterism of Bharaṇī, the drinking of liquor (āsava) is auspicious. [Verse 50] Regarding "in Pauṣṇa" (Pauṣṇe): in these asterisms, the commencement of dancing is excellent. In Ka (Revatī), Pauṣṇa (Revatī), Puṣya, the pair of Vasus (Dhaniṣṭhā and Śatabhiṣaj), Ravi (Hasta), Maitra (Anurādhā), all three of the Uttaras, Indra-bha (Jyeṣṭhā)—in these, dancing and the commencement of dance are excellent.

One should observe the auspicious moment (*muhūrta*) for the commencement of a dance performance by river-dancers in a dance hall. The *laghu* asterisms are Hasta, Puṣya, Citrā, and Abhijit; the *mṛdu* asterisms are Mṛgaśīrṣa, Citrā, Revatī, and Anurādhā. Under the pair of *śrī* asterisms, namely Śravaṇa and Dhaniṣṭhā, and under the *dhruva* asterisms—Rohiṇī and the three *uttarās* (Uttaraphalgunī, Uttarāṣāḍhā, and Uttarabhādrapadā)—an audience with the king (*nṛpatīkṣaṇa*) or the beholding of the monarch is excellent. On a Saturday (*śanivāra*), during the *dhruva* asterisms, the protection of servants is recommended when one’s physical constitution is stable.

In the first three [nakṣatras], in Ārdrā, there is the serpent; in Maghā, Indra; in Jyeṣṭhā, the snake; in Mūla, the hundred [of stars]; in the southern [Bharaṇī], the vessel (āsaka) is auspicious. By the word *āsava*, one generally means grape-wine (*drākṣāsava*), clove-wine (*lavaṅgāsava*), and honey-wine (*madhukāsava*). It provides the auspicious moment for kings. Because of his state as a yogin, he observes the conjunction of those [planets] at the auspicious moment. In the *Ratnamālā* as well, the asterisms for the commencement of liquor are stated at the beginning.

And likewise: "In the constellations of Raudra, Pitrya, Vāruṇa, Pauruhūta, Yāmya, and Nairṛta, as well as in the three known as the eastern ones, the commencement of liquor is declared to be excellent by the ancient experts in time. (50) The auspicious moment for the remarriage of an unchaste woman (vṛpalī) occurs in the asterisms of Puṣya, Aśvinī, Svāti, Hasta, Anurādhā, Dhaniṣṭhā, and Śravaṇa; on the days of Wednesday, Saturday, Thursday, or Friday; when the strength of the Moon is favorable; and when it is free from the Riktā and Ku-yogas. One should draw that diagram starting from the direction of Indra (the east), with the Sun's position moving sequentially through the signs.

In the constellations of Dāne (Pūrvaphalgunī), Śubha (Śatabhiṣaj), Anila (Svātī), and Viṣaya (Jyeṣṭhā), as well as those mentioned by Jñāti (Anurādhā), one should resort to the Dharma. (Verse 51) Regarding Pauṣṇa (Revatī) and the others: in these yogas—namely, Pauṣṇa (Revatī), Aśvinī, Anila (Svātī), Hasta, Maitra (Anurādhā), Vasu (Dhaniṣṭhā), Āra (Maṅgalavāra/Mars day), Arka (Ravivāra/Sun day), Jīva (Guruvāra/Jupiter day), and Bhṛgu (Śukravāra/Venus day)—this refers to the union with another man of an unchaste woman who desires other men, or of a widow with another man. Which ones? In Pauṣṇa (Revatī), Aśvinī, Anila (Svātī), Hasta, Maitra (Anurādhā), Vasu (Dhaniṣṭhā), Āra (Mars day), Arka (Sun day), Jīva (Jupiter day), and Bhṛgu (Venus day).

In that regard, when the strength of the moon is present and both the moon and [the weekday] are auspicious, one should avoid the *riktā* dates, evil yogas, and [the lunar days of] *vyatīpāta*, *vaighṛti*, *mṛtyu*, *kāṇa*, *yamaghaṇṭa*, and so forth. On that wheel (*cakra*) consisting of five spokes, one should write three [asterisms] each, starting from the sun's [natal] asterism and proceeding in order from the directions of Indra (East) and the center. Among those, the asterism of the moment (*muhūrta-bha*) is not auspicious in the southeast (*āgneyī*), nor is it auspicious in the northwest (*anila*); in the other directional divisions, the asterism of the moment should be known as excellent.

The *viṣaya* (region), the *deśa* (country), the *jñāti* (kin), and one's own *varṇa* (caste)—in this sequence, that which is called the *dharma* of the *jñāti* should be followed. Thus it has been said: "A wise man should never disregard the customs of his family and country based on the perspective of the scriptures; for the root of those [customs] is the great unrighteousness (*adharma*) resulting from the loss of the Vedic branches due to the defect of decline. Therefore, in whatever family the remarriage of a widow is appropriate, in that very region and according to that *dharma*, the act should be performed by them through the aforementioned methods. [End of section on] the results of planetary transits (*gocara-phala*).

In the eleventh house, all nine planets bring about gain. In the sixth house, Mercury, Mars, and the Sun cause lameness; Venus, Jupiter, and the Moon are capable of causing loss; and Saturn causes loss when situated in the twelfth house, except when it is in an even sign. Jupiter is auspicious in the sixth, eighth, twelfth, second, seventh, and fifth houses from the natal ascendant; however, in marriage, he is honored in the fourth, seventh, and tenth houses, provided he is not afflicted by others. (52) Regarding the word "lābhe": all nine planets, when situated in the eleventh house, become givers of profit.

Saturn (Śani) and Mars (Bhauma), the son of the Earth, are auspicious in the sixth and third houses. The Sun (Arka/Sūrya) is excellent in the third, sixth, and tenth houses. The Moon (Śaśī/Candra) is excellent in the third, first, seventh, sixth, and tenth houses. The other planets [are likewise considered] according to their positions. (Third, Sixth, Tenth = 3 | 6 | 10; Third, First, Seventh, Sixth, Tenth = 3 | 1 | 7 | 6 | 10)

7.6.10. Mercury (Budha) is excellent in all houses except the twelfth (vyaya). Venus (Bhṛgu) is excellent in the second, fourth, sixth, eighth, tenth, and twelfth houses; however, Venus is not auspicious in the sixth, tenth, seventh, and eleventh houses. Jupiter (Ījya/Guru) is excellent in all other houses except the seventh, ninth, second, fifth, and eleventh. [In the first house: Birth—

This result regarding the field of activity (*gocara-phala*) is to be understood by calculating from the natal ascendant (*janma-rāśi*). In marriage (*udvāha*) or wedding (*vivāha*), Jupiter (*ījya*) is auspicious when situated in the third, first, sixth, tenth, third, or eleventh houses from the *kula* [ascendant]; thus says the *Muhūrtadīpaka*. Having performed worship, the moment (*lagna*) should be fixed; as it has been said: "When Jupiter is in the sixth, the birth [sign], the third, or the tenth house..."

"An extensive worship should be performed for the girl; this is declared to be auspicious. This refers to the transit of the planets (*gocara*) and the results thereof. That auspicious result which has been declared is bestowed only when the planet is not pierced (*vedhita*) by others. In this context, the piercing of planets during their transit is also mentioned; as it is stated in the *Ratnamālā*: "The Sun situated in the eleventh (*lābha*), third (*vikrama*), tenth (*kha*), or sixth (*śatru*) houses is declared to be auspicious."

"If the planet Saturn (5) does not pierce the fifth, ninth, fourth, or twelfth houses from the *khecarī* [ascendant], then it is auspicious. Here, Saturn does not pierce [these]. "If the Moon, occupying the seventh, first, sixth, eleventh, tenth, or third house, bestows auspicious results, provided it is not pierced by the wise planets situated in the second, fifth, twelfth, eighth, or fourth house. (2) In this case, there is no conjunction of Mercury with the Moon in the fourth house.

When Mars (Kuja) is auspicious, occupying the third (3), eleventh (11), or sixth (6) house, it is not pierced by any planets situated in the twelfth (12), fifth (5), or ninth (9) houses, provided that even this son of the Sun (Mars) is not pierced by the lord of the ninth house. (3) Saturn (Śani), however, is not pierced by the Sun (Sūrya). When Mercury (Jña) is auspicious, occupying its own (2), fourth (4), sixth (6), eighth (8), tenth (10), or eleventh (11) house, it is certainly not pierced when it is not afflicted by planets situated in the fifth (5), third (3), ninth (9), first (1), eighth (8), or twelfth (12) houses. (4)

For Mercury, there is no piercing by the Moon. When Jupiter is situated in the second (2), eleventh (11), ninth (9), fifth (5), or seventh (7) house, it is auspicious; provided it is not pierced by the sky-travelers [planets] in the twelfth (12), eighth (8), tenth (10), fourth (4), third (3), or seventh (7) houses. Venus is considered auspicious when not pierced in the sixth (6), eighth (8), ninth (9), twelfth (12), eleventh (11), or first (1) house. [Saturn is auspicious] when not pierced in the eighth (8), seventh (7), first (1), tenth (10), ninth (9), fifth (5), eleventh (11), or sixth (6) house.

"Simultaneously with the three *sthakhecara*s. (6) Venus is to be considered in this manner: when a planet is in the piercing position (*vedhaka-sthāna*) and the piercer (*vedhaka*) is in the planetary position (*graha-sthāna*), then there is a leftward piercing (*vāmavedha*); at that time, the planets bestow auspicious results. Thus it has been said: "In this way, when the planets are possessed of piercing in their *gocara*, they do not grant good results."

"By the method of leftward piercing (*vāmavedha*), even these inauspicious [planets] bestow abundant auspicious results. (1) Here, since the piercing generally occurs facing forward, it is so stated for all cases. And it is said: "Wherever a planet is from its own sign, and where a planet is from that planet, the piercing there should be known as ineffective; [only when pierced] as previously described does it certainly yield the stated result. (12) [The section on] Travel by Boat.

In the *Pūrvās* (the three *Pūrvā* constellations), in *Śravaṇa*, in the two *Mṛdu* signs, in light signs, on a favorable lunar day, on a Friday or a day with clarified butter (*ājya*), when malefic planets are in their periods of growth (*upacaya*) and benefics are not in the sixth or eighth houses—then travel by boat is excellent. Furthermore, it is auspicious during the northern solstice (*uttarāyaṇa*), under the asterisms *Maghā*, *Ājya* (Punarvasu), and *Śravaṇa*; and likewise in the *Mṛdu* signs, when the Moon is in a movable sign, and when the Sun is free from the influence of *Kāraka* and *Jihma*. (53) Regarding "In the *Pūrvās*" and so forth: under these planetary configurations, travel by boat—that is, the setting out of a vessel—is most excellent.

The boat should be set in motion when the sun is in the three *pūrva* constellations (*Aśvinī*, *Bharaṇī*, *Kṛttikā*), in *Śravaṇa*, in the two *mṛdu* constellations (*Anurādhā* and *Mṛgaśīrṣa*), in the *laghu* constellations (*Hasta*, *Punarvasu*, *Puṣya*, *Aśleṣā*), in *Punarvasu*, on a favorable lunar day (*iṣṭa-tithi*) excluding the *riktā* days (4th, 9th, and 14th), on a Friday, or on a day of Venus, the Sun, or Jupiter; and when the ascendant is in the *upacaya* houses (3rd, 6th, 10th, or 11th), while malefic planets (*khala*) are in the *jyārikhāya* houses (1st, 2nd, 4th, 7th, 8th, and 12th) and benefic planets (*sadgraha*) are in the favorable houses (3rd, 6th, 10th, and 11th), being free from the sixth and eighth houses.

Immediately thereafter, upon hearing the *uttarāyaṇa* [northern transit] and the *ājya* [full moon], her maintenance—the casting of wealth into the middle of the boat—should be performed. Having gone to that shore at a time free from the Sun, Mars, and Saturn, and at a time devoid of the *riktā* lunar days, one should perform the business during a *mṛdu* (mild) asterism and a *cara-laghu* (mobile-light) *muhūrta*. "Whatever wealth has been employed here in a vessel that is neither common, fierce, nor of terrible aspect..."

"Because of the statement, 'That [result] is never obtained as certain,' the practice [of calculation] regarding mixed, slow, and sharp [periods] is forbidden. (13) The Ship-Wheel (*naukācakra*): One should assign six asterisms to each of the well-clothed and tree-rooted [sections] from above; one in the *paṭhāṇa*; nine on the back side; one at the mouth of the *kumuḍu*; and six for the load in the middle.

54. From the solar mansion (the asterism occupied by the Sun), [one should count] on the surface of the prow of the ship, on the stern, on the deck, and in the middle; those who know the results have declared that success is found at the prow, while danger is spoken of here in the case of the "boat-wheel" (potacakra) at the stern. Regarding "each one": starting from the solar mansion (bhāsvaddhiṣṇya), which is the asterism occupied by the Sun, one should write down one asterism for each [position]: at the well-cloth (kūpavastra)—where the word *kūpa* refers to the central timber of the ship and *vastra* refers to the sail (*śaṭi*)—one should write one asterism there for each [spot].

From the base of the mast and from the base of the well, one should place six asterisms each toward the north; on the *paṭhāṇa* (the main beam), one *paṭhāṇa* each; at the *naukā-maṇḍana-kāṣṭha* (the wood for the boat’s ornamentation), there is one; at the *sukāṇa* (the rudder) and also at the station where the helmsman sits, one; on the back and the sides, nine each—the back, the side, and the back-side; in those two sides, three each; on the back, three—thus making nine; at the *uḍumukha* (the bow of the boat), one; at the *naumukha* (the mouth of the boat), one; at the *kuṃ* (the hold), one; and at the *bhṛti-sthāna* (the place of the crew), six are to be placed.

In that regard, among the nine asterisms [of the ship's wheel], those situated on the surface of the prow (*paṭhāṇa*), on the face of the stern (*naumukha*), on the peak (*śikhara*), at the top of the mast (*kūpamastaka*), and on the deck (*tala*) are not desired. Success is found in the *sukāṇa* (the rudder) and in the center; thirteen asterisms in the center grant success. In the *paṭhāṇa* (known as *śaṭha*), there is danger. Thus, the results in this ship-wheel have been declared by those who know the fruits. 14. [End of section] B. The four circles.

The asterisms Āgneya (Kṛttikā), Sada (Punarvasu), Pitrya (Maghā), Abha (Anurādhā), Miśra (Śatabhiṣaj), Bhaga (Pūrvaphalgunī), Ajāṅghribha (Pūrvabhādrapadā), Vāyavya (Svātī), Mṛga (Mṛgaśīrṣa), Daravāyu (Uttarāṣāḍhā), Aditibha (Śravaṇa), Tvaṣṭṛ (Citrā), Aryamā (Uttaraphalgunī), Koṇḍu (Viśākhā), Aindra (Jyeṣṭhā), Maitra (Anurādhā), Kāma (Aśleṣā), and Aiṃdra (Jyeṣṭhā) bestow desired fruits. Likewise, the four Vaiśvānara asterisms (Pūrvabhādrapadā, Uttarabhādrapadā, Revatī, and Aśvinī) do so. Furthermore, during the three types of portents—celestial, atmospheric, and terrestrial—the two circles [of the moon] are not auspicious. [Specifically,] Mūla, Upāntyabha (Abhijit), Sarpa (Āśleṣā), Varuṇa (Śatabhiṣaj), Ambu (Pūrvaphalgunī), Āśe (Uttaraphalgunī), Jya (Puṣya), and the asterism belonging to Varuṇa (Śatabhiṣaj) [are also unfavorable]. Regarding the phrase "Āgneyam": during the threefold portents characterized as celestial, atmospheric, and terrestrial, the pair of circles [of the moon] is not [auspicious]. It is *sat* (existent/true).

What is that? The last [asterism], Revatī, is Pitrya; Yamabha is Bharaṇī; Mitra is Kṛttikā and Viśākhā; Bhaga is Pūrvāphālgunī; Ajāṅghri is Pūrvābhādrapadā. This is the Āgneya Maṇḍala (the circle related to Fire); there is no affliction (*upasarga*) in this circle connected with Agni. Furthermore, Mṛgavana is Vāśva; Aditibha is Citrā; Tvāṣṭra is Uttarāphālgunī; Āryaman is Hasta; and Mārka is Mṛgaśīrṣa, Aśvinī, Svātī, and Punarvasu. This is the Vāyavya Maṇḍala (the circle of Wind); even there, no portent (*utpāta*) occurs.

Anurādhā belongs to Mitra; Rohiṇī, Jyeṣṭhā, and the four stars beginning with Uttarāṣāḍhā belong to Indra; thus, Uttarāṣāḍhā, Abhijit, Śravaṇa, and Dhaniṣṭhā constitute this circle of Indra, which bestows desired results. Mūla, Pūrvābhādrapadā, Āśleṣā, Śatabhiṣaj, and Pūrvāṣāḍhā belong to Varuṇa; Ārdrā and Puṣya belong to Īśa; this is the circle of Varuṇa, which bestows desired results during portents.

And so it has been stated in the *Amṛtakuṃbha*: "The group of Āryaman, Citrā, Aditi, Bhanda, Vāśvi, Svāti, and the Sun's asterism (Pūrvaphalgunī) belongs to Anila (Wind). Yāmya (Bharaṇī), Ajapada (Pūrvabhādrapadā), Agni (Kṛttikā), Bhaga (Pūrvaphalgunī), Pauṣṇa (Revatī), Maghā, Viśākhā, and Hutabhuj (Kṛttikā)—this is the group of Agni. Toyeśa (Śatabhiṣaj), Ahirbudhnya (Śravaṇa), Rakṣas (Āśleṣā), Ambu (Pūrvāṣāḍhā), Pūṣan (Uttaraphalgunī), Sapa (Mūla), Aiśāna (Jyeṣṭhā), Vāruṇa (Śatabhiṣaj), and Agni (Kṛttikā) are the asterisms. Maitra (Anurādhā), Brāhma (Rohiṇī), Vaiṣṇava (Śravaṇa), Vāsava (Dhaniṣṭhā), Indu (Mṛgaśiras), Vaiśva (Uttaraphalgunī), and Aindra (Jyeṣṭhā)—this is the group of Indra. Abhijit is the Bhava-group. [The] result [is as follows].

If there is an upasarga (obstruction) from the group of Vāyu, then at that time the wind becomes exceedingly fierce; the earth may be drenched with blood, and great unrighteousness shall prevail even toward the king. (1) In the case of the group of Agni, there is a momentary flash of light; eye disease, dysentery, loss of land, and the provocation of strength-destroying [fevers]; cows yield little milk, trees become fruitless, and there is miscarriage among pregnant women. (2) Cows are endowed with abundant milk and other qualities, trees flourish, and the subjects are possessed of security, prosperity, and abundance of food.

When the group of Varuṇa (the Water-lord) is afflicted with obstacles, there will be abundant clouds that release copious water. When the group of Mahendra is afflicted, there is happiness among women, and all the subjects become joyful. One should know that when Maghavan (Indra) rains as much as desired, the earth possesses an abundance of crops. Thus [ends verse 55]. (16) [Now follows] the consideration of Venus's setting (*śukrāsta*) and other such matters: When Jupiter has entered the sign of Virgo, or when Jupiter is situated in Leo, or while Jupiter is still in its childhood state, or when Venus is in retrogression (*aticāra*), or when Venus has reached old age.

The *sīmantonnayana* (parting of the hair), the feeding of food, as well as the ritual implements—the ivory, the lotus, and the safflower—should always be worn by women; this is the supreme duty, and it must never be neglected. 57. Iti.

When the Sun is in Aries or Taurus; when the Moon is in Sagittarius or Pisces; when Jupiter has entered its period of decline (*apāya*) or is in its southern course (*dakṣiṇāyana*); when Jupiter is situated in Leo; or when Jupiter is in its childhood (*bāla*), its setting (*asta*), its retrograde motion (*aticāra*), or has reached old age (*sthaviratā*)—at such times, the *sīmantonnayana* (parting of the hair), the *annaprāśana* (first feeding with solid food), and the wearing of ornaments by women—including jewelry, ivory ornaments, pearls, saffron-dyed garments, and so forth—should never be performed here.

By the principle of elimination (*pāriśeṣya*), everything [inauspicious] has been stated. Thus it is said in the *Jyotirmīmāṃsā*: "When Jupiter is situated in its sign of debilitation (*nīca*), retrograde (*vakrita*), or in *aticāra* motion; or when it is young, old, or set (*asta*); then renunciation (*saṃnyāsa*), sacrifice, pilgrimage, observances, rituals, ear-piercing, initiation (*dīkṣā*), the tying of the sacred thread (*mauñjībandha*), the marriage ceremony for women, and the consecration of temples and deities—these must be diligently avoided by the virtuous when Jupiter is in the sign of the Lord of the Thirty (Jupiter) or in the sign of Hari (Venus). In this regard, the *Muhūrtadīpaka* states:

Regarding the retrogression of Venus, he states: "In the seven instances of dancing, traveling, entering a house, [eating] old food, and at the conclusion of the *prāśana* ceremony, as well as for the auspicious entry of the bride, there is no [restriction regarding] the 'infancy' (*mauḍhya*) of Jupiter and Venus. By "entry of the bride," one means the entry into the home of a woman who has already been married. Also, in the *Nirṇayasiddhānta*: "Whether after sunset or before sunrise, if Jupiter is in his 'old age' or 'infancy,' or if Venus is in his 'old age' or 'retrogression,' one should not perform this rite."

From the caulakarman until the end of the marriage ceremony, the rites for the bridegroom and the bride—including the commencement of vows, their conclusion, the offering of the great gift (mahādāna), and the departure—must not be performed by those who are ineligible. (1) Furthermore: "When Jupiter or Venus has set, during their childhood or old age, or during an intercalary month (malimluca), one should not perform the commencement or conclusion of vows, nor the tying of the sacred thread (mauñjībandhana). Nor should one perform the consecration of ponds, wells, tanks, and the like, sacrificial rites, the entry into a new house, the gift of a cow, or festivals for the installation of deities and grand celebrations."

One should not perform [these rites] during intercalary months (*mala-māsa*), nor when Jupiter or Venus are eclipsed or have set. Regarding that, O King, a specific rule has been stated concerning Jupiter being in Leo: "During the retrograde motion (*vakrāticāra*) of Jupiter, one should avoid twenty-eight days; when he is in Leo, five signs (*navāṃśaka*); when he is in Capricorn, exactly five; and when he is in his sign of debilitation (*nīca*), five signs. For those living between the Godāvarī and the Yamunā, rites such as vows, marriage, and shaving should always be performed there; for there is no other sacred ford (*tīrtha*) superior to the waters of the Godāvarī. 1.

All rites beginning with *garbhādhāna* (conception) and ending with *prāśana* (the first feeding), must be performed in all regions even when Jupiter is situated in Leo. ||2|| On the northern bank of the Godāvarī and the southern bank of the Bhāgīrathī, marriage and other such ceremonies must not be performed when Jupiter is situated in Leo. ||3|| Due to the attainment of a bridegroom or excessive delay, or because of famine and regional upheaval, marriage is auspicious on the southern bank of the Gautamī even when Jupiter is in Leo. ||4|| Even when Jupiter is in Leo, one should diligently avoid him when he is stationed in the *Maghā* constellation.

"Except in the Leo portions, marriage and other rites are ordained. Sixty days or six months have been declared by Bādarāyaṇa; in the northern transit (uttarāyaṇa), rites for the gods and rites for the ancestors are both permitted. Thus, when Jupiter transits [into another sign], the year becomes deficient (luptābda). And so it has been stated in the *Muhūrtacintāmaṇi*: "In signs other than Taurus, Aries, Virgo, and Aquarius..."

4. With Commentary. When Jupiter, having retrograded, enters a sign other than the one previously occupied, then that year is considered "eclipsed" (vilupta) and is strictly censured for auspicious rites, provided it falls within the interval between the Revā and the Asuranimnagā [rivers]. All such matters are to be inferred from this. The Epilogue of the Work: The first [section] contains various compositions of faultless verses, intended for those of discerning minds, clearly set forth for the purpose of observing the worldly conduct of people during the Saptarṣi cycle.

"Of the first ones," etc. The poet Mahādeva composed this *Muhūrtadīpa*. Of what characteristics was he? He was the son of that illustrious Kānhajit-vāḍava, whose feet were worshipped by the kings of the glorious Raivata mountain—Raivata being another name for Raivataka (Girnar). Such was Kānhajit-vāḍava; his son was [Mahādeva]. His offspring was [the author].

Having done what did he compose this? Having reflected upon and deliberated with his own mind in various ways upon the faultless poetic compositions of the foremost teachers—Varāha, Śrīpati, Lalla, Trivikrama, and others—and having considered their numerous treatises such as the *Ratnamālā*, *Trivikrama*, *Śataratnakośa*, *Vyavahāraprakāśa*, *Sajjanavallabha*, *Vṛttaśata*, and *Muhūrtatattva*; for what purpose? For the sake of providing the rules for observing the daily conduct and auspicious moments (*muhūrta*) for all people.

But the perception of the conventional usage of objects occurs only by means of this [method]. Thus, having composed it in seven pentads of verses, he made it a "lamp of moments" (muhūrtadīpa). Just as there is a wick in a lamp, so here the wick consists of fifty-seven characteristics; by that being the cause [of illumination], [the work was composed].
